Moreover, in the entire Federation you have the same problem occurring with the Croats. The relations between the Serbs and the Muslims have the same troubles as existed between them and the Serbs because the Croats felt that they are being dominated over and the international community did establish that there was this domination being enforced, that something had to be done, constitutional amendments, a revision of the Dayton Accords, et cetera. So my convictions today are even firmer than they were back in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will try to put questions to you now which will allow you to give me a yes or no answer. You also mention the incident at Vase Miskina Street here as something that was a monstrous crime. Do you still stand by this position today that this had an impact on you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. As things stand today, this is clearer than it was at the time. I was following the testimony of the lady who is an explosives expert here before the Tribunal and her expertise was very compelling. What made me suspicious of it at the time - and this involved a house that was a hundred metres away from mine - was that the Sarajevo TV crew appeared there at an incredible speed. Even at the time, suspicions arose of it having been pre-staged, but even later new evidence emerged that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we stop here? It goes too far. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3646, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 76 and I will try to phrase my questions as yes/no questions. On page 76 in connection with Exhibit 6356, an OTP exhibit, you state that General Halilovic could not be fully trusted when it comes to the representation of the military situation. Was General Halilovic to be fully trusted when he spoke about the sufferings of the Muslims and other events in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff suggested that Dr. Kecmanovic was informed by Halilovic of the sufferings of the Muslims, and Mr. Kecmanovic said that Halilovic couldn't be trusted because he lied a lot about the military situation, so I asked him a question whether he was to be trusted on other things. That's not leading. That's taking up an issue from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, it would have been better if he had just asked the second part of the question without making reference to the first, but it's not really a leading question if it's only limited to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I tend to agree, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall we ask the witness to answer or shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Rephrase, rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was General Halilovic at Presidency meetings to be fully trusted regarding information about events in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the suffering of the people and the victims?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have mentioned that his almost daily statements at Presidency meetings were one-sided and biased. When he spoke about the sufferings of the -- of Muslim civilians, this is blown out of proportion, and on the other hand when he spoke about the successes of the army that he led, he also would exaggerate incredibly. Even the Muslim and Croatian members of the Presidency were distrustful and Izetbegovic himself once pointed out to him not to exaggerate and said, "If you were really so successful militarily, we would be controlling all of Bosnia-Herzegovina by now."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 66 you were asked what Pale demanded. Did the Dayton accord grant us special links with Serbia that we had demanded?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: There is no need to even answer that. Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was suggested that the Serb side - or specifically I claimed that we couldn't continue living with the Muslims in one state. Did that equally refer to the SFRY and the independent Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb option - and when I say "Serb," I say it with full consciousness that it wasn't only the position of the SDS but also of my party and it was also the opinion of other Serbs who weren't members of any party - the first option was that Bosnia-Herzegovina should stay part of Yugoslavia. But everything else was imposed by force because the legitimate and legal Serb option was ignored. Everything that happened subsequently is merely a consequence of that position of the sides in the conflict which was first political and then also military.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like to let you know that the Chamber wishes to rise at 3.45 sharp today -- 2.45.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll try to cut things short, and I kindly ask for Professor Kecmanovic to answer yes or no whenever he can, although I'm not allowed to ask leading questions the way the OTP did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please start over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice whether in me and the rest of the Serbian leadership and the leadership of the Serbian movement there was a difference in the attitude toward the Muslims we considered fundamentalists and the Muslims we didn't consider fundamentalists?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, there was a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 60 you spoke out against genocide and you said that this didn't refer to any specific side. The document is P6353. Did you mean a specific perpetrator or one specific side are responsible of committing genocide?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you said "movements of population," that the OTP linked to ethnic cleansing, did you mean forcible removal of population -- forcible resettlement of population or transfer --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What did you mean? You can ask -- simply ask in that way: What did you mean by "movement of population," "massive movement of population"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 53, what did you mean by "massive movement of population"?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: "Massive movement of population" is a very broad term. It is something that has continued in Bosnia-Herzegovina even after the end of the war and not only in Bosnia-Herzegovina but in all of former Yugoslavia. Movements of population have been present since the Second World War. A great percentage of Serbian and Croatian population left Bosnia-Herzegovina in peace time after 1945. This process is taking place even now, after 1995. I did not place that in the context of the use of force because in that case it's called something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have on one part of the screen P06352 and on the other part D220.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Dr. Kecmanovic, did you notice in the Serb leadership or any official Serb factor intentions or inclinations or desires to transfer population or an inclination toward ethnic purity?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: The people I communicated with - and that's you, Plavsic, Krajisnik, Koljevic - I never observed that. It seems to me that at one point when there was a discussion about the division of territory and all sides took part in that and all international agreements from Cutileiro's before the war and up until the ones after the war were all about that, and I don't know why this is being stigmatised. Even the international factors were in favour of such a solution and now it's become something odious, but I would like to remind of your suggestion, I think, your proposal that in places where a Muslim or Croatian -- where the Muslims or the Croats are the majority in that territory, that there should be sub-autonomies for places in that territory with a definite majority. I believe that was applied to something in northern Bosnia. So there should be safety for everybody through the system of sub-autonomies.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get page 2 on the right half. And on the left side there is the platform that I issued on the 22nd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please focus on paragraph 5. Can you tell us how this tallies with your understanding of our attitude toward the use of force?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that paragraph 5 is almost identical to what the Prosecutor mentioned from what I had stated at a Presidency meeting in Sarajevo. In other words, an advantage obtained by force will not be recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 2, or rather, on the right-hand side can we see item 4, sub-item (c), if we could just see that. We can remove this left half of the screen. Next page, item 4(c). "The recognition of the legal authorities of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its institutions in its entire territory." Can you tell us how you understood this and under what conditions these authorities could be legal without the legitimate representatives of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item (c) --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, you -- the last part of your question was leading. What is your question? Could you reformulate your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Kecmanovic, please, how do you understand this? What is the Muslim side pleading for? What legitimate authorities would those be in all of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: I understood this to mean some sort of authorities in accordance with what was mentioned at the beginning, that would come about only by all three sides agreeing again, the same way it happened in Dayton. That's the only way for Bosnia to be preserved, and I'm afraid the chronic impossibility to reach such agreement can only result in a separation. Who was supposed to take part in this? Maybe you and I together if I had stayed in the Presidency or only the Pale leadership, that's open to speculation. But it's certain that the Serbian people would have to have its say. But if this had been like this at the beginning, I'm sure that there would have been no civil war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And my last question: Did they, that is the Muslim-Croatian coalition, understand this item (c) the same way as you do regarding the legality of authorities at this moment?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC
utterances.text: The Bosniaks, I'm afraid, no; I'm not sure about the Croats. I think that they were in favour of that but not the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor Kecmanovic. If there were more time, I would have more questions but given the time I will finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Kecmanovic. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague. Please have a safe journey back home. We'll adjourn but there's one thing. The Chamber is still considering the motion by Mr. Tolimir requesting to suspend the subpoena and to allow to appeal on the decision. Given the circumstances, it seems prudent to reschedule his evidence which is scheduled for next week to a further date pending the outcome of the decision -- the request. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kecmanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you for the good wishes for my return to Belgrade. I have a request if you would let me say good-bye to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic must have heard this statement of yours. It is not consistent with our practice.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: But it was approved in Krajisnik case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not at this time. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of June, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.51 p.m.,
